context.claim: The training rows come from complete life sequences, but the hidden rows are one truncated snapshot per unit.  Most training mass sits in the long-remaining-life region that the hidden protocol never scores, so the model is fitted to the wrong part of the target distribution.
context.change: Re-weight every training row by the importance ratio between a bounded uniform remaining-life prior (a training window narrower than the selection view) and the training RUL density, tempered by a square root.  No row is duplicated, the feature schema is untouched, and prediction still needs only ``inputs``.
context.falsifier: If the RMSE on the bounded-RUL validation view does not fall, the long-RUL mass was not the problem.
context.expected_effect: Late-life RMSE falls; full-sequence RMSE may rise slightly.

applied.sample_weight: sqrt importance: uniform RUL<=150 / training RUL density

context.decision: the hypothesis is confirmed: late_rmse moved from 38.5199 to 33.9115 (full rmse 52.2253 -> 57.4199, within the +12.0% guard)
